newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks storm to new highs at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks storm to new highs at open.

text.p: Australian shares stormed to a record high at the open on Friday as Wall Street surged again and base metals prices strengthened.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 14.8 points to 2,437.8.
The benchmark reached a high of 2,438.4 points before easing back. This surpassed the previous record high of 2,429.2 reached on January 9, 1997.

"The market is pretty enthusiastic. It's driven largely by the positive sentiment coming out of the U.S. at the moment, particularly on the back of producer price index data that came out yesterday," said dealer Scott Mailer of Daiwa Securities.
"There was very little noise from the data and that has calmed fears of the so-called inevitable correction in the U.S."

Mailer was confident of a strong finish but he cautioned the market may ease later if SPI futures ran too far ahead. "You might see our market come off a little in the afternoon depending on how far the SPI gets ahead. If the premium gets out much further you may see some volatility in the market."

The resources sector had the best of early gains, with the major miners all showing strong gains, while among energy stocks Woodside continued to benefit from strong investor interest in the sector. Its shares hit a high of A$10.00 (US$7.80) early.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to two, while about 37 percent of stocks traded steady.
